evals.name: csv-batch
evals.prompt: I've got fullTesting.csv sitting in this folder with 6 cameras on it (mostly Hikvision/LVT units, one Axis, one Dahua we're not sure about). Can you run the camera audit against it and tag the report 'JulyCheck'?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes CSV batch mode, builds a run_audit.py --csv <path> --tag JulyCheck invocation, explains it needs to launch in a separate console window for credential prompts (does not ask for username/password in chat), and flags that the Dahua row and the blank-IP row will be skipped/flagged rather than guessed.

assertions.text: Identifies this as CSV batch mode, not single-camera mode
Constructs a run_audit.py command using --csv pointing at fullTesting.csv and --tag JulyCheck
Does not ask the user to type a camera username or password into the chat
Explains that credentials will be entered in a separate/new console window rather than inline
Notes the Dahua row will be flagged/skipped (Missed Cameras) rather than guessed as Axis or Hikvision
Notes the row with a blank IP will be skipped

evals.name: single-camera-diagnostic
evals.prompt: Can you check camera 192.0.2.44? It's one of our Axis units and I just want to see what analytics rules are configured on it before we ship it out.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes single-camera mode, builds a run_audit.py --ip 192.0.2.44 --manufacturer axis invocation without asking for unnecessary info, and explains the separate-console-window credential step.

assertions.text: Identifies this as single-camera mode, not CSV batch mode
Constructs a run_audit.py command using --ip 192.0.2.44 --manufacturer axis
Does not ask the user to type a camera username or password into the chat
Explains that credentials will be entered in a separate/new console window rather than inline
Does not ask the user to produce or locate a CSV file for this single-camera request

evals.name: snowflake-no-csv-yet
evals.prompt: We need an analytics audit for unit TDC14016 for a client walkthrough tomorrow. I don't have a CSV yet -- what's the fastest way to get this done?
evals.expected_output: Points to the Snowflake query for pulling that unit's IP/manufacturer into a CSV (adjusting the WHERE clause to TDC14016), rather than guessing an IP or skipping straight to run_audit.py without one.

assertions.text: Provides a Snowflake SQL query (or clearly points to one) filtered for unit TDC14016
Does not fabricate or guess an IP address for the camera
Explains the exported CSV needs an IP column (and ideally MANUFACTURER) before the audit tool can run
Does not ask the user to type a camera username or password into the chat
